candidates.detail: Server drop constructs a cuboid using physical dimensions as full extents, then a compound child at local -anchor_offset and spawns the dropped item with identity rotation and a dynamic rigid body. The pickup path later reads the item Transform but computes its center as translation minus the unrotated local offset. Range and terrain line-of-sight therefore use that helper position. The client selects scene items using GlobalTransform::transform_point(-anchor_offset), then sends a mapped Pickup action on release. The client and native compound pose apply rotation to the local offset; the server helper does not.
candidates.catalog_case: For a projected non-parametric catalog halberd, dimensions are [0.16,2.1,0.08], grip-to-tip is 1.9 and local anchor offset is [0,-0.2,0]; current projection retains those catalog values if no accepted instance geometry replaces them and the source validity checks admit the resulting physical fields. With unit scale, a synchronized unparented item origin at (0,0,0), and an assumed +90 degree rotation about X, its local box center (0,+0.2,0) transforms to (0,0,+0.2). The server helper instead uses (0,+0.2,0). An actor at (0,0,2.15) is 1.95 m from the rotated center but approximately 2.159 m from the helper; the two-metre client targeting admits the former while server range rejects the latter. Given an empty hand, a clear client line of sight, a valid camera and no competing selection, the client can select and submit this target, conditional on the remaining action and network gates. This is source geometry and arithmetic only; no item, rotation, pickup, physics or runtime result was observed.
candidates.safeguards: The dropped item starts at identity rotation, where both center calculations coincide. A vertical catalog offset is unchanged by yaw alone; the example requires pitch or roll. A dynamic rigid body can rotate in principle, but this trace does not establish that the particular supported item reaches the assumed pose, that client/server transforms are synchronized, or that the user sees the example. Server actor authority, sequence, revision, held-item and validity checks remain intact. The existing source assertion covers a nonzero offset without rotation; it was read, not run.
candidates.connected_scope: Catalog/parametric physical dimensions and local anchor, dropped compound collider and dynamic world pose, replicated client GlobalTransform and target selection, mapped request identity and optimistic concurrency, server world-space range and terrain line of sight, inventory transfer.
candidates.proposed_repair: After the complete audit and implementation authorization, project the same admitted local center through the captured authoritative item pose for both server range and line of sight; use the existing frame/physical owners and preserve identity-rotation drop construction, client selection and legitimate actor/sequence/revision safeguards. Establish unit-scale and parent/physics synchronization policy before choosing the exact transform owner.
